meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: not later than the next regular payday
facts.summary: Pennsylvania: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Separated Employes. Whenever an employer separates an employe from the payroll, or whenever an employe quits or resigns his employment, the wages or compensation earned shall become due and payable not later than the next regular payday of his employer on which such wages would otherwise be due and payable.
facts.source_title: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act of 1961 P.L. 637 No. 329, Section 5 (PA DLI copy)
facts.source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry

facts.value: Employers must report all newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days of the hire date. (23 Pa.C.S. § 4392(d)).
facts.summary: Pennsylvania new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Employers must report all newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days of the hire date. (23 Pa.C.S. § 4392(d)).
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Employers must report all newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days of the hire date. (23 Pa.C.S. § 4392(d)).
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.value: Regular paydays designated in advance; wages due within 15 days after the pay period ends unless a contract or trade custom sets otherwise
facts.summary: Pennsylvania pay frequency rule: Regular paydays designated in advance; wages due within 15 days after the pay period ends unless a contract or trade custom sets otherwise.
facts.evidence_quote: All wages, other than fringe benefits and wage supplements, earned in any pay period shall be due and payable within the number of days after the expiration of said pay period as provided in a written contract of employment or, if not so specified, within the standard time lapse customary in the trade or within 15 days from the end of such pay period.
facts.source_title: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Section 3 (PA DLI copy)
facts.source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry

facts.summary: Pennsylvania is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Pennsylvania base new employer UI rate: 3.8220%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. DOL value equals the state's published total: PA DLI lists the 2026 newly liable non-construction rate as 3.8220% including the 9.2% surcharge (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dli/resources/for-employers-and-educators/how-to-file/uc-tax/yearly-tax-highlights).

facts.value: 1.4190% to 10.3734% total (includes 9.2% surcharge and 0.60% additional contributions)
facts.summary: Pennsylvania 2026 experience-based UC contribution rate range: 1.4190% to 10.3734% total.
facts.evidence_quote: Range of Rates for Calendar Year 2026 The minimum experience-based contribution rate is .014190 (this includes the 9.2 percent Surcharge and the 0.60 percent Additional Contributions tax). The maximum experience-based contribution rate is .103734 (this includes the 9.2 percent Surcharge and the 0.60 percent Additional Contributions tax).
facts.source_title: UC Tax Yearly Tax Highlights (Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry)
facts.source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry
facts.notes: Rate basis: total. Basic rates alone run 0.75% to 8.95% (DOL Significant Provisions). Employees also pay 0.07% UC withholding on all gross wages, no cap (same PA page).

facts.summary: Pennsylvania state unemployment taxable wage base: $10,000 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance

facts.summary: Pennsylvania 2026 total new employer UC rate (non-construction): 3.8220% (includes the 9.2% surcharge).
facts.evidence_quote: The newly liable non-construction employer contribution rate is .038220 (this includes the 9.2 percent Surcharge only, because the 0.60 percent Additional Contributions tax does not apply to newly liable employer contribution rates).
facts.source_title: UC Tax Yearly Tax Highlights (Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry)
facts.source_publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry
facts.notes: Newly liable construction employers: 10.5924%. Employees also pay 0.07% UC withholding on all wages (employee cost).
